description:
Ben Fatih Gedikoğlu. Manisa'da Robotik Kodlama ve Bilişim Teknolojileri öğretmeniyim. NASA Space Apps Challenge, FLL, WRO, Scratch Cup ve TÜBİTAK ve NASA SPACE yarışmalarında öğrencilerimizin projelerini geliştirmelerinde yol gösteriyorum. 2025 NASA Space Apps'te takımlarımızla 5. ve 14.'lük elde ettik. 

Robotik, yapay zekâ, uzay teknolojileri ve inovasyona ilgi duyan; araştırmacı,hikaye yazabilen, yaratıcı ve takım çalışmasına yatkın kişilerle birlikte proje üretmek istiyorum.
summary: Deep Space Legacy is a science-fiction story that follows astronaut Atlas on a journey through Earth, the Moon, Mars, and the Sun. Blending real NASA space missions with an imaginative future, the story explores humanity’s survival, scientific discoveries, and the importance of preserving knowledge for future generations.
details:
The year is 2025…

Humanity believed it had secured its future on Earth, the planet where life had flourished for millions of years. Science and technology had advanced; humans had walked on the Moon, sent robots to Mars, and designed spacecraft to study the Sun up close. But the greatest threat humanity would ever face came from the darkness of space.

Astronomers detected a gigantic celestial object traveling toward Earth from the outer regions of the Solar System. Scientists named it APOCALYX. Initial calculations suggested that it was approximately 100 kilometers in diameter and moving at 200 kilometers per second. An object of this size and speed striking Earth could have devastating, planet-wide consequences.

Observatories around the world repeated their calculations again and again. Space agencies, scientists, and engineers searched for ways to prevent the collision. But as the time remaining before the potential catastrophe grew shorter, none of the proposed solutions proved sufficient.

And then the dreaded moment arrived.

APOCALYX struck Earth.

Enormous tsunamis rose across the oceans after the impact. Shock waves spread across continents. Powerful earthquakes, fires, and dust storms engulfed the planet. Particles thrown into the atmosphere reduced the amount of sunlight reaching the surface. Plants were damaged, agriculture collapsed, and food chains began to break down. Earth was facing a catastrophe on a scale humanity had never experienced before.

It was a scene reminiscent of the Chicxulub impact that occurred approximately 66 million years ago in Earth's history.

In the aftermath of the disaster, communication networks and energy infrastructure failed one by one. Survivors struggled to find clean water and safe shelter. Using the spacecraft, life-support systems, and scientific infrastructure at their disposal, space agencies prepared an emergency evacuation plan. It was impossible to save everyone. The priority was to protect the survivors and preserve humanity’s accumulated knowledge.

Experienced astronaut Atlas was part of this operation. After working at the evacuation center, Atlas boarded one of the last spacecraft and looked out the window at Earth. The planet that had once shone with deep-blue oceans and lush green forests was now disappearing behind smoke and clouds.

The young passenger beside him asked, “Atlas, will we ever be able to return?”

Atlas did not answer for a long time. At last, he said, “I don’t know. But there is one thing I do know: humanity’s story must not end here. We will find a way to survive.”

Their first destination was the Moon. Earth’s closest celestial neighbor might serve as a temporary refuge. As the spacecraft left Earth’s orbit, they were leaving behind not only their home, but all their memories as well.
